record_body:
Account summary
- Northbridge is evaluating Redwood for an AI-assisted support-agent experience: live “agent copilot” chat + real-time suggested replies + post-chat summarization.
- Primary concern is streaming experience consistency (TTFT + steady token cadence) under bursty concurrency during business hours.
- They have an existing internal LLM service (self-hosted vLLM) but are hitting tail latency + operational burden; considering Dedicated (VPC) to keep data isolated.

Workload / requirements (from discovery + POC scoping)
- Workload type: streaming chat completions (agent copilot), plus secondary summarization batch jobs.
- Traffic shape:
  - High streaming mix: ~80–90% requests streaming.
  - Prompt lengths: mixed; typical 800–2,500 input tokens (chat history + retrieved snippets). Long tail up to ~12k tokens during escalations.
  - Output lengths: 150–600 tokens typical; occasionally 1,200+ for “explain steps” responses.
  - Concurrency: baseline 150–250 concurrent streams; spikes to 500+ during incident surges (they used the phrase “all hands on deck hours”).
- Targets (stated, not yet validated):
  - TTFT p95: < 450ms (hard preference), p99 < 900ms.
  - TPOT/streaming cadence: stable enough that the UI doesn’t “stutter” (they measure “tokens/sec perceived”; want no multi-second stalls).
  - End-to-end latency for non-streaming summarization: p95 < 6s for ~800 out tokens.
  - Error rate: <0.2% non-2xx; strict timeouts on the frontend.
- Quality constraints: “We can accept slightly worse writing style if latency is consistent.” Interested in fallbacks (smaller model variant) when under load.
- Model preferences:
  - Interested in a strong chat model w/ tool calling and JSON mode for structured actions.
  - Want options for long-context performance; also open to smaller model + retrieval if perf is better.

Security / compliance notes
- Deployment: VPC required (customer data in prompts). “Hosted public endpoint is a non-starter for us right now.”
- SSO/SAML required for Console access.
- Audit logging required for admin actions and key inference events.
- Retention controls: wants a clear stance that prompts/responses are not stored by default; if logs are needed for debugging, must be opt-in and time-bounded.
- KMS integration requested (customer-managed keys).
- Data residency: prefers US-only for initial rollout.

Baseline / benchmarking alignment (key thread)
- They asked for “reproducible performance numbers we can take to our architecture board.”
- Plan is to map their workload to Redwood’s Q1’26 representative traffic shapes:
  - Streaming, mixed prompt lengths, bursty concurrency, warm-cache and cold-cache runs.
  - Include long-context streaming shape (where TTFT/first-chunk handling matters) and mixed-tenant batching pressure (simulate multi-queue fairness).
- Requested artifacts: methodology summary, variance budget, and the run metadata (hardware SKU, driver/CUDA/runtime build, region) so they can compare apples-to-apples over time.

Timeline / activity log
- 2026-01-14: Record created after inbound request (pricing + VPC question).
- 2026-01-22: Discovery call — clarified streaming UI constraints and concurrency spikes; discussed Dedicated vs Private options.
- 2026-02-06: POC scoping call (Fireflies: ff-2026-02-06-poc-scoping-representative-load). Action items captured: provide representative load plan + confirm model shortlist.
- 2026-02-13: Shared draft benchmarking plan referencing Q1’26 baseline suite + traffic-shape taxonomy; Northbridge requested “attestation-ish” language (we clarified what we can/can’t provide).
- 2026-02-21: Follow-up email: Northbridge security team sent questionnaire sections on retention/audit logging/KMS; asked for sample audit log fields.

Open questions
- Final model shortlist for POC: long-context model vs smaller model w/ more aggressive retrieval. Need Applied ML input on quality regression risk if we use fallback variants.
- Whether to run in single region first (us-east) or dual-region active/standby; they worry about “regional wobble” and want guidance.
- Their own TTFT measurement: currently client-clock; we need to align definitions (server TTFT vs client observed first-token). Potential confusion flagged.

Next steps (internal)
- SE (Claire) to translate their stated distributions into the workload suite config + request a baseline-style run (Dedicated VPC-like isolation). Include streaming TTFT/TPOT and tail latency panels.
- Coordinate with Runtime perf baseline effort: use the locked Q1’26 runner outputs + artifact stamping so we can re-run if hardware/driver changes.
- Pull in Observability (Aisha) for dashboard expectations + ensure telemetry matches client-perceived TTFT (avoid the “first chunk timestamp” mismatch we’ve seen elsewhere).

Next steps (customer-facing)
- Send: (1) benchmark methodology one-pager (definitions for TTFT/TPOT, run structure, warmup/cooldown), (2) proposed workload mapping table, (3) security posture summary for VPC + retention controls.
- Schedule results review w/ Northbridge Eng + Security: walk through p95/p99 streaming behavior, explain variance, and discuss fallback/routing policy under surge.

Internal notes / quotes
- “It’s not the average latency that kills us, it’s the stalls.”
- “We can’t have a model that looks fast in a demo and then falls apart at 400 concurrent streams.”
- They are explicitly comparing against OpenAI Enterprise and a DIY vLLM stack; price sensitivity is secondary to consistent p99 + isolation.
